title: Apify Homepage Teardown: Jan 2020 to Jun 2026
h1: How Apify rewrote its homepage over 6 years
metaTitle: Apify Homepage CRO Teardown — Jan 2020 to Jun 2026
description: A CRO teardown of Apify's homepage from Jan 2020 to Jun 2026 — what changed in headline, section headings, CTAs, navigation, and what SaaS teams can study from it.
excerpt: Apify's homepage didn't just get updated. The headline, section headings, CTAs, navigation all shifted in a consistent direction between Jan 2020 and Jun 2026. This teardown maps what changed, when, and what the patterns may suggest.
author: Wael Aouididi
authorBio: SaaS Growth Marketer and fractional growth lead. I help B2B SaaS founders diagnose landing page, CRO, positioning, and analytics leaks before scaling traffic.

analysisBlocks.label: Jan 2020 — original state
analysisBlocks.heading: The original: product-led messaging
annotations: H1 opens with: "Extract data from any website" — direct product statement.
Visible section headings include: "Turn any website into an API", "How can Apifyhelp your business?", "Products".
Navigation includes: "Free store", "Get quote" — product category framing.
Section headings later removed include: "Turn any website into an API" and "How can Apifyhelp your business?".

analysisBlocks.label: Apr 2022 — mid-transition
analysisBlocks.heading: Mid-period: signs of a structural shift
annotations: Visual similarity to the previous snapshot: 93.5% — a moderate visual change.
H1 in this snapshot: "The most powerful web scraping and automation platform".
New section headings appearing: "Hundreds of ready-to-use tools", "Use Apify for various use cases".
Changes across this period appear incremental rather than a single redesign event.

analysisBlocks.label: Jun 2026 — current state
analysisBlocks.heading: Today: updated positioning
annotations: H1 now reads: "39,044 tools for your AI" — updated value proposition.
New section headings include: "Not just a web scraping API", "Take your Actors beyond the open web", "Build and deploy reliable scrapers".
CTAs no longer present include: "Browse all actors".

lessonCards.title: Your H1 signals which buyer you are targeting
lessonCards.body: The headline changed from "Extract data from any website" to "39,044 tools for your AI". The framing of your H1 is one of the clearest signals of which buyer you are targeting and what you expect them to do next.

lessonCards.title: Navigation is a positioning statement
lessonCards.body: Navigation items changed from "Free store", "Get quote", "Docs" to "Get started", "Log in", "Product". The labels your navigation uses reveal what you think your visitor is trying to decide — and who that visitor is.

lessonCards.title: Section headings reveal what the team thinks buyers care about
lessonCards.body: 7 section headings were added and 2 removed between Jan 2020 and Jun 2026. New headings include "Not just a web scraping API" and "Take your Actors beyond the open web". Headings that disappeared include "Turn any website into an API" and "How can Apifyhelp your business?". The pattern of what gets added and removed is one of the clearest signals of how a team is re-prioritizing its value proposition.

lessonCards.title: Incremental changes compound into a brand shift
lessonCards.body: Across 5 snapshots spanning roughly 6 years, no single update here was a dramatic overhaul. The end state looks very different from the start because small, consistent changes in the same direction accumulate. This is worth studying if your own homepage has been drifting without a clear direction.
